# Plot the contours of a two-dimensional item

Draws the response surface of
[`prob_mirt()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/irtexplorer/reference/prob_mirt.md)
seen from above, as labelled contour lines of equal probability, with
the zero lines of both axes, a thick line at one probability (usually
halfway between the asymptotes) and, optionally, the item vector as a
blue arrow. Both axes have the same scale, so the angle of the arrow is
true.

## Usage

``` r
plot_mirt_contour(
  theta1,
  theta2,
  z,
  nlevels = 10,
  level = NULL,
  arrow = NULL,
  xlab = NULL,
  ylab = NULL
)
```

## Arguments

- theta1, theta2:

  Abilities on the two dimensions.

- z:

  Matrix with one row for each value of `theta1` and one column for each
  value of `theta2`.

- nlevels:

  Approximate number of contour levels.

- level:

  Probability of the thick line, or `NULL` for none; every piece of it
  is drawn, and none when the grid does not reach it.

- arrow:

  Item vector from
  [`item_vector()`](https://sedzinfo.github.io/irtexplorer/reference/item_vector.md),
  or `NULL`; it is drawn when it lies inside the plotted grid.

- xlab, ylab:

  Titles of the axes; `NULL` labels the abilities with the Greek letter
  theta, as theta1 and theta2.

## Value

A `plotly` object.

## Examples

``` r
theta <- seq(-4, 4, length.out = 50)
plot_mirt_contour(theta, theta, prob_mirt(theta, theta), level = 0.5, arrow = item_vector())
```
